script.title: Real camera footage of a rover landing on Mars
script.description: On 18 February 2021, NASA landed the Perseverance rover inside Jezero Crater on Mars. Cameras captured the entire landing sequence from atmospheric entry to touchdown.

shots.narration: This is real footage of a 1,025-kilogram rover descending toward the red surface of Mars.
On 18 February 2021, the spacecraft entered the Martian atmosphere at 20,000 kilometres per hour.
A 21.5-metre parachute deployed while the craft was still traveling faster than sound.
The journey from the top of the atmosphere to touchdown took about seven minutes.
A rocket-powered descent stage hovered and lowered the car-sized vehicle on 7.6-metre cables.
Cameras on the back shell, descent stage, and rover recorded the ground rising below.
After touchdown, the descent stage cut the cables and flew off to crash at a safe distance.
Radio signals took eleven minutes to reach Earth, so the landing was complete before mission control knew.
This was the first time a landing on another planet was filmed by its own cameras.
